lesson.title: Review Day: Your Capstone Civics Proposal
lesson.subject: social-studies

contentBlocks.text: This week you built every piece of a real capstone civics project. Let's put it all together!

Quick review: choose a real, specific, local issue (Day 1). Identify who has real authority over it (Day 2). Develop a specific action plan (Day 3). Consider real challenges and other perspectives (Day 4). Combine your issue, identified authority, action plan, and challenge-response into one complete capstone civics proposal.
Great work this week — you built a complete, real capstone civics proposal, ready to actually carry out! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review issue choice, authority research, action planning, and perspective-taking
Combine all four into one complete written capstone civics proposal
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child assemble their complete capstone civics proposal.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a real, ready-to-carry-out capstone civics proposal!
differentiationTips: Struggling: it's fine if the proposal is short — focus on genuinely combining all four pieces rather than length
Ready for more: ask the child what they'd need to do next to actually send or present this proposal in the real world
This is the week's synthesis moment — a real, usable civic-action proposal the child can genuinely follow going forward, not just a review exercise
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended synthesis activity — check that the proposal genuinely combines all four elements from this week (the specific issue, the correctly identified authority, the drafted action, and a thoughtful challenge-response) into one coherent, usable civic-action proposal.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's capstone-civics-project thread before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session, producing a genuinely usable final artifact rather than just a review.
